error: On the dashboard the PL and DE cards carry each other's labels; values and claim ids are untouched.
warning_texts: The check plan has no deterministic rule binding a displayed label (such as a country code on a dashboard card) to the population of the claim it shows, so a swapped label passes every configured release check.

gate_release_machine reports all 21 rendered numbers bound and gate_release_document reports all 15 checks PASS, which disagrees with what a reader of release/dashboard_data.json cards[2] and cards[3] actually sees.

audit/check_plan.json lists gate_release_document rules claims_rendered and caveats_rendered under accepted_unproven because their breaker runs failed with FileNotFoundError, so that gate's PASS has never been shown to fire.

gate_release_document evidence/checks.json contains no recompute_*, claims_recomputed, component_sum or column_identity comparison, so at this stage no machine check recomputes a displayed number from source and the numeric verification of the release rests on the registry chain and on earlier gates
release/report.md states in words that country figures sum to the headline but does not print the sum; the three shown figures do add exactly to the shown 35,741.52.
The refund-rate caveat on both surfaces uses the identifier 'paying_customers' rather than plain words; the basis is disclosed but reads as a field name.
summary: Every number shown on report.md, dashboard_data.json and the manifest is exact against the claim register and metrics registry (country parts sum to the headline 35741.52, gross 40235.02 minus refunds 4493.50 equals the headline, 27/57 = 0.473684 on the paying-customer basis), and report.md labels, caveats and population are correct and visible; but release/dashboard_data.json swaps the country labels: cards[2] reads 'Net revenue DE (EUR)' while showing CLM-NET-PL, and cards[3] reads 'Net revenue PL (EUR)' while showing CLM-NET-DE, so a dashboard reader attributes Poland's net revenue to Germa
